defects.title: is_service_role() / raw != NULL-collapse authorization pattern — 4-file audit, 2 live exploits found and fixed
defects.detail: public.is_service_role() returns SQL NULL (not false) when neither JWT claim is set, and a raw `auth.uid() != p_user_id` guard evaluates NULL for any unauthenticated (anon) caller — both collapse a NOT-wrapped AND-chain guard to NULL, which PL/pgSQL's IF treats as false, silently bypassing the RAISE EXCEPTION. Live audit of the LIVE function definitions (not migration-file text) across all 4 originally-flagged files found: (1) get_referral_stats — migration text vulnerable but superseded by a later migration using IS DISTINCT FROM, and anon has no EXECUTE grant anyway — CLEAN, no action. (2) get_user_activation_score — had a prior partial fix (COALESCE around is_service_role) but still carried the raw auth.uid() != p_user_id leading term, and anon DOES have EXECUTE — CONFIRMED LIVE EXPLOITABLE via direct curl (HTTP 200, real data, arbitrary UUID, zero auth) — FIXED. (3) get_user_engagement_stats — fully unpatched, anon-executable — CONFIRMED LIVE EXPLOITABLE the same way — FIXED. Both fixes applied via migration 20260822225616 (IS DISTINCT FROM + COALESCE), re-verified with a second identical curl showing HTTP 400 Access denied post-fix.
defects.next_action: Fix applied to live production DB, verified, and the migration file committed/pushed via PR #49. The repo-wide sweep for other instances of this pattern has now been done (item 8, building the Semgrep rule) -- see QNT-DEFECT-015, which found and fixed 2 more real instances (get_subscription_summary, get_referral_stats) and adds a permanent CI gate so this bug class can't regress silently again.

Root cause is no longer ambiguous: every commit since b7a5068e (23 commits, HEAD=8b7faf11) fails the GitHub 'Vercel' status check with an explicit message -- 'Git author AIWMCX must have access to the project on Vercel to create deployments' (target_url is a live Vercel team-invite link for team jeltovbogdan-7049's projects). The last SUCCESSFUL deploy (741bbbe7) was authored by gpt-engineer-app[bot]; every commit since was authored as AIWMCX, which the invite link itself confirms lacks Vercel team membership -- Vercel's Deployment Protection blocks git-triggered deploys from non-team-member authors by design. Directly proved with the live bundle: fetched https://www.aiwmcquantis.com's current JS asset and grepped it -- 0 matches for claim_content_admin_if_allowlisted/isContentAdmin/requireContentAdmin (the content_admin feature shipped in PR #47, commit 20ff6af2, earlier this same session), but 1 match for the OLD claim_admin_if_allowlisted and 16 matches for OLD requireAdmin. The live frontend is unambiguously the pre-b7a5068e build. Full evidence and required-action detail in docs/VERCEL_DEPLOY_PIPELINE_FINDING.md.
defects.next_action: ROOT CAUSE NARROWED (2026-08-23, direct evidence from the user's Vercel dashboard, not inference): the block reason on every deployment is 'The deployment was blocked because the commit author did not have contributing access to the project on Vercel. The Hobby Plan does not support collaboration for private repositories.' The account is on Vercel's Hobby plan, which cannot add ANY collaborator to a private-repo project at any settings level -- options 1/2 below (team invite / relax deployment protection) are NOT available on this plan; only options 3 or 4 work. Confirmed via the full Deployments list that this has blocked EVERY deployment since Aug 11 (dozens, not the originally-estimated 23), and that the separate backend-only production-deploy.yml pipeline has continued deploying successfully throughout -- this is purely a frontend static-bundle problem, zero effect on data. Because git history is cumulative, a SINGLE successful deploy of current main HEAD supersedes all historical blocked entries; none need to be individually replayed. Two real options: 1) Grant GitHub identity AIWMCX access on the Vercel team via the invite link (requires upgrading to Vercel Pro first -- Hobby cannot grant this at all). 2) Relax Vercel Project Settings -> Git -> Deployment Protection (also requires Pro -- not available on Hobby). 3) .github/workflows/vercel-production-deploy.yml is a manual one-click CLI-based deploy (VERCEL_TOKEN auth, bypasses the git-author check entirely by deploying via API token instead of git identity -- works on Hobby plan) with a built-in smoke test + fidelity gate + auto-rollback. FIXED 2026-08-23: its preflight script was scoped to 'all' secrets, hard-requiring STRIPE_SECRET_KEY/STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET/DEEPSEEK_API_KEY even though grep confirmed none of this workflow's actual steps (nor verify-deploy.sh/vercel-rollback.sh) ever read them -- those are backend runtime secrets belonging to the separate, already-working production-deploy.yml job. Rescoped to `bash scripts/preflight-secrets.sh vercel`, which only checks VERCEL_*/VITE_* (6 total: VERCEL_TOKEN, VERCEL_ORG_ID, VERCEL_PROJECT_ID -- new; VITE_SUPABASE_URL/PUBLISHABLE_KEY/PROJECT_ID -- already present). Verified locally: `bash scripts/preflight-secrets.sh vercel` exits 0 with only those 6 set. User has the 3 new secrets ready to add. 4) Upgrade to Vercel Pro (user's cost/business decision, not attempted here). After any fix: force-redeploy main HEAD and re-run the same live-bundle grep to confirm the fix lands, then build the frontend build-metadata endpoint (Workstream A) so this stops requiring bundle forensics. IMPORTANT CORRECTION (2026-08-23, later same day): this defect's scope is the FRONTEND (Vercel git-integration bundle) only. A SEPARATE workflow, .github/workflows/production-deploy.yml, auto-triggers on every CI-green push to main; it builds the frontend and runs a non-blocking post-deploy smoke test, but its actual deploy actions are backend-only (Supabase DB migrations + edge function deploys) using only the 3 already-present secrets (SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN, SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD, VITE_SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID) -- it does not perform the Vercel deployment itself, that remains Vercel's own git integration. Confirmed via gh run list that it has run and succeeded 3 times today (2026-08-23; no claim made about runs before today) (all 4 jobs green, including the hard-fail schema-contract check), independent of and unaffected by the frontend git-author block. Backend fixes shipped this session (e.g. the email_funnel_30d migration) were applied directly via the Supabase MCP tool and are already live in the database regardless of this workflow; no supabase/functions/*.ts code was changed this session, so there is nothing new for this workflow to have deployed. Re-confirmed live: https://www.aiwmcquantis.com still shows the pre-fix copy ('Multi-model verified', not 'cross-checked') as of this correction, proving the frontend is still stale. Until fixed: PR #47's frontend half (Content Studio/Autoposter access for the 2 newly-granted accounts) AND every frontend-only fix from this session's PRs #59/#60/#61/#62/#63 are NOT live -- treat all of them as reopened for the purpose of 'is this actually protecting users right now', not done.

defects.title: Analytics parity gap between persisted analyses and completion funnel events — magnitude confirmed real, not fully explained
defects.detail: Two independent measurements, two different rolling windows, both show a real gap: 2026-08-18 measured 11 completion events / 27 analyses (~59% gap) in its 30-day window; this capture measured 30 completion events / 46 analyses (~35% gap) in its own 30-day window. Neither figure supersedes the other -- do not report this as 'the gap improved from 59% to 35%,' that would be comparing two different windows as if they were a trend. The honest finding is: a material, currently-unexplained under-reporting gap exists in every measurement taken.
defects.next_action: Task chip task_46a94f92 already covers the code-path audit (which analysis-creation paths call trackAnalysisCompleted() and which don't) — execute that before drawing further conclusions from either number. IMPORTANT reframing (2026-08-23, QNT-DEFECT-005): both prior parity measurements were computed over the undifferentiated user base, which is 84% test-fixture accounts and has 0 EXTERNAL_REAL analyses at all. Re-run this parity check joined through the new public.user_cohorts view filtered to EXTERNAL_REAL before drawing any further conclusion -- a parity ratio over test/founder activity says nothing about instrumentation quality for real users, and with 0 real analyses to date there is currently no real-user data to even compute a real-user parity ratio from.

Live-verified against all 44 real auth.users rows: 4 EXTERNAL_REAL, 2 FOUNDER, 1 STAFF, 37 TEST -- 84% of the entire user base is test/QA fixture accounts. Cross-checked against real usage data, which is the actual point of this classifier: of those 4 EXTERNAL_REAL users, 0 have EVER completed a single analysis (0 of 142 analyses system-wide belong to a real external user, all-time, not just in a recent window), and only 1 has ever held a paid subscription -- Plus, and it already expired (current_period_end 2026-08-11, the exact same account fixed in QNT-DEFECT-019 for the current_period_end entitlement bug earlier this session). This directly and for the first time answers GTM top-20 question #1 ('how many EXTERNAL_REAL people completed an analysis in the last 7 days') -- the answer is 0, and extending the window to all-time doesn't change it. Reclassified P2->P0: this isn't a measurement-infrastructure gap anymore, it's evidence that zero real product-market validation has occurred to date, which changes the urgency of nearly everything else on the GTM priority list.

defects.title: OpenTelemetry tracing pilot built, verified, and wired into 2 call sites -- but structurally inert everywhere until a tracing vendor/endpoint is chosen
defects.detail: Workstream E previously had zero tracing of any kind. Built supabase/functions/_shared/otel.ts: a hand-rolled OTLP/HTTP JSON span emitter (deliberately not the full @opentelemetry/sdk-trace-* SDK, whose AsyncLocalStorage-based context propagation is a poor fit for short-lived Deno edge isolates), following the exact 'direct HTTP POST, fire-and-forget, never throws' pattern already proven safe by the existing Sentry integration in _shared/logger.ts. Verified with real, committed, re-runnable evidence (supabase/functions/_shared/otel.test.ts, `deno test --allow-net --allow-env`), not just code review or deleted scratch scripts: 4 tests cover spec-correct OTLP JSON shape against a real mock collector, correct ERROR-status + error-propagation on failure, true no-op behavior when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is unset (every environment today), and correct OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS parsing. Two real defects were found and fixed during CodeRabbit review, not just style nits: (1) the first draft cached env vars in module-level `const`s, which is a genuine 'warm isolate keeps stale config' bug for Supabase's isolate-reuse model, not just a test artifact -- fixed by reading env vars fresh on every call; (2) fetchDatabaseBenchmarks (the wrapped function at one of the 2 pilot call sites) caught its own DB errors internally and always returned [], so the span could never report ERROR on a genuine failure -- fixed by re-throwing on the direct-query error path while leaving the cache layer's own resilience (benchmark-cache.ts) untouched, and the caller's pre-existing try/catch still falls back to [] exactly as before. Also added OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS support (standard OTel env var, 'key1=value1,key2=value2' format) since nearly every commercial OTLP backend requires an auth header. `deno check` passes clean on otel.ts, otel.test.ts, and the full 4512-line analyze-business/index.ts. `bun run lint` shows 0 errors / 319 warnings, verified by identity (grepped the full lint output for the 3 changed/new file names -- zero matches) not just count, that zero new lint debt was introduced. Wired into exactly 2 already-isolated async call sites in analyze-business/index.ts -- no other function touched, no internals of the core financial-calculation logic touched.
defects.next_action: This is genuinely a pilot, not a rollout -- next steps require a product/business decision this session can't make: 1) Choose a tracing backend/vendor (Honeycomb, Grafana Tempo, Datadog, etc.) and provision OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT as a Supabase Edge Function secret. 2) Once chosen, extend traced() wrapping to more call sites incrementally (the AI narrator call, calculateStrictFinancials, other edge functions) -- deliberately not done broadly yet since there's no backend to view the traces in, and touching more of the core engine without that payoff isn't justified. 3) Separately and NOT yet resolved this pass: it's unknown whether the backend's OWN Sentry integration (_shared/logger.ts's SENTRY_DSN, a server-side secret, distinct from the frontend's VITE_SENTRY_DSN found dark in QNT-DEFECT-012) is actually configured in Supabase Edge Function secrets -- no tool available this session lists edge-function secret names, and no CI secret-sync step references SENTRY_DSN the way CRON_SECRET has one, which is circumstantial evidence it may be unset too, but this is NOT confirmed either way and should not be assumed.

defects.title: Property-based (fast-check) invariant tests added for src/financial/* -- mutation-tested to confirm they actually catch regressions, and caught a real flaw in their own tolerance model along the way

Added src/__tests__/financial-invariants-property.test.ts targeting the REAL, production-imported modules (calculateInvestmentPayback, calculateCacPayback, calculateCvp) rather than the mock reimplementation financial-engine.test.ts already uses for convenience. 23 properties across both payback functions (identical cumulative-crossing algorithms, tested with a shared battery: no numeric sentinel ever leaks, negative principal always INVALID_INPUTS, empty series always INSUFFICIENT_INPUTS, horizonMonths always matches series length, VALUE months always bounded within [0,horizonMonths], NOT_ACHIEVED_WITHIN_HORIZON implies cumulative genuinely never recovered, VALUE reconciles against an independently-written reference recomputation, and monotonicity -- increasing any single month's cash flow never increases payback) and calculateCvp (never throws for any finite input combination, always returns a contractually-typed status, negative inputs always INVALID_INPUTS, and 3 algebraic reconciliation checks against its own contract). defects.title: LockedNumericPayload -- built and wired the missing contract; CanonicalResult confirmed to already exist as BusinessAnalysisResult, not a gap
defects.detail: Item 11 ('AnalysisSnapshot/CanonicalResult/LockedNumericPayload contracts'). AnalysisSnapshot was already confirmed live in item 10's investigation. Before writing anything for the other two, read src/lib/analysis-contract.ts and src/types/analysis.ts: BusinessAnalysisResult (types/analysis.ts) already IS the canonical result -- a mature, extensively-consumed full-analysis shape (financial_analysis, business_plan, marketing_plan, confidence_score, validation, assumption_graph, etc.) read by hooks, PDF export, the document mapper, and golden-vector tests. No new 'CanonicalResult' type was needed or created. LockedNumericPayload was genuinely missing: analysis-snapshot.ts's numericOutput field was Record<string, unknown> -- any shape, any subset of fields, no embedded process versioning, no canonical rounding -- and its one real call site (analyze-business/index.ts) passed an untyped inline object literal with the exact same 14 fields every time, discovered by reading that call site directly rather than assuming. Built supabase/functions/_shared/locked-numeric-payload.ts: a strict LockedNumericFields type matching those exact 14 fields, a lockNumericPayload() constructor that canonically rounds every field (2dp, matching the .toDecimalPlaces(2) convention already established throughout src/financial/*.ts), embeds engineVersion/formulaRegistryVersion INSIDE the hashed content (a locked payload is tied to the process that produced it, not just its values -- the same numbers hash differently under a different engine version, by design), computes a self-describing SHA-256 hash over a canonical (fixed field order, rounded) serialization, and genuinely deep-freezes the result at runtime (Object.freeze, not just a TypeScript readonly annotation a caller could still mutate through). Added verifyLockedPayloadIntegrity() for later reconciliation use. Wired into analysis-snapshot.ts (numericOutput retyped from Record<string,unknown> to LockedNumericPayload; numeric_output_hash now reads payload.hash directly instead of redundantly re-hashing the whole object) and the one real call site in analyze-business/index.ts, which now builds the payload via lockNumericPayload() before calling emitAnalysisSnapshot -- a genuinely surgical change to that 4500+-line file, touching only the exact object-literal call site, nothing else. Verified with a real, committed, re-runnable Deno test suite (9 tests: hash determinism, hash changes on any field/engineVersion/formulaRegistryVersion change, floating-point noise below the rounding precision does NOT change the hash, throws on non-finite fields rather than silently locking garbage, genuine runtime immutability -- not just compile-time readonly, tamper detection via verifyLockedPayloadIntegrity, and field-order independence). Type-checking the wiring surfaced a real pre-existing looseness: financial-calculator.ts declares npv3Years as optional (number | undefined) even though its one unconditional return path always assigns a concrete number -- rather than silently defaulting to 0 (which would fabricate a real NPV value), used `?? NaN` so the payload's existing non-finite-value guard throws (caught non-fatally, exactly the same fire-and-forget safety guarantee as before) if that invariant is ever actually violated.

defects.title: pg_net extension-in-public advisor finding -- investigated, found to be a false positive / already-attempted-and-rejected fix, not a real actionable issue
defects.detail: The 4th real finding from the same advisor sweep (extension_in_public). Investigated the isolated fix path (ALTER EXTENSION pg_net SET SCHEMA extensions) before applying it, per this entry's own original next_action. Found supabase/migrations/20260726225622_enable_pg_net_extension.sql already documents that this exact schema-move was tried when pg_net was first installed (2026-07-26) and Postgres itself rejected it: 'cannot move extension into schema net because the extension contains the schema' -- pg_net's own install script creates its member functions in a schema literally named `net` regardless of what schema the extension's own catalog entry (pg_extension.extnamespace) is filed under. All 5 real call sites (grep-confirmed) use unqualified `net.http_post(...)`, resolving via the `net` schema itself, not `public`. The advisor's flag is therefore a metadata-only artifact of Supabase's own pg_net packaging (extnamespace='public' even though the functions live in `net`), not a real security or hygiene issue, and re-attempting the suggested fix would just reproduce the same Postgres error already hit and documented 4 weeks ago.
defects.next_action: None -- reclassified NOT_APPLICABLE rather than left open indefinitely. If this advisor finding is ever revisited, start from the existing note in 20260726225622_enable_pg_net_extension.sql rather than re-deriving this from scratch.

defects.title: Flagship sample report's own P&L table does not reconcile -- revenue minus its own itemized costs is $1,800/mo, not the $11,800/mo displayed everywhere; a second narrative line implies a SECOND OPEX total, and a fragility bullet ('rent = 28% of OPEX') implies a THIRD
defects.detail: Surfaced via a pasted GTM/sales-readiness report from a differently-connected session, cross-checked directly against src/data/sampleReport.ts rather than accepted on faith. Confirmed by direct arithmetic: the Year-2 steady-state P&L table (page 7) lists COGS $8,236 + Rent $9,400 + Staff $6,200 + Utilities $2,764 = $26,600 in costs against $28,400 revenue -- an unambiguous $1,800/mo net profit. The table instead displays 'Monthly net profit: $11,800' (also the headline metric card, meta description, and HEADLINE_METRICS.monthlyProfitY2). A separate summary sentence on the same page claims '$28.4k MRR against $16.6k blended OPEX, leaving $11.8k of monthly net' -- a SECOND, different OPEX figure ($16,600) that is also inconsistent with the itemized table ($26,600) and is itself mathematically impossible given Rent+Staff alone ($15,600) leave only $1,000 of headroom for COGS+Utilities before even reaching $16,600. A THIRD data point ('Largest fragility: location rent at $9.4k/mo (28% of OPEX)', page 2) implies a further different total OPEX of ~$33,571 (9,400/0.28). Three internally-contradictory OPEX totals exist in one document ($26,600 itemized / $16,600 summary sentence / ~$33,571 implied by the 28% figure), and the 18-month payback headline (the report's actual cover metric) is only numerically plausible if the true monthly profit is close to $11,800 (11,800 x 12 months post-breakeven is approximately $141,600, matching the $142,500 investment almost exactly) -- meaning the itemized cost table, not the $11,800 profit figure, is most likely where the fictional business's numbers were never actually run through arithmetic by whoever authored this content. This is NOT a code bug (it is authored example data) and NOT something this pass attempted to silently 'fix' by inventing a new self-consistent cost breakdown -- every combination of the 4 line items tested (keeping the heavily cross-referenced $9,400 rent fixed) requires COGS+Staff+Utilities to total just $7,200 combined, which is not achievable with any individually plausible values for a specialty-coffee-shop COGS/staffing model without further invented assumptions. Flagging precisely rather than guessing.
defects.next_action: Requires a person to rebuild this fictional case's numbers holistically (revenue ramp, COGS%, staffing, rent, and the resulting payback timeline) so all three OPEX references and the payback headline reconcile -- not a mechanical fix. This is the single highest-visibility 'accuracy and trust' item in the entire public product: it is the flagship proof artifact shown on the landing hero to every cold visitor. Until rebuilt, do not send outbound traffic to the homepage funnel that leads with this sample as proof of depth.

defects.title: 2 confirmed-false security/compliance claims on the live /security page and homepage trust strip -- checked against actual schema and live HTTP response headers, source fix committed but NOT yet deployed
defects.detail: Followed up on the deal-snapshot report's flag that GDPR/CCPA/AES-256/HSTS/admin-logging claims needed verification against deployed infrastructure. Checked src/pages/Security.tsx (a real, live route) directly against the database schema and live HTTP headers: (1) 'phone numbers and billing identifiers are stored encrypted at the column level' -- queried information_schema.columns directly: only user_brand_profiles.phone_encrypted (bytea) is actually column-level encrypted; profiles.phone and auth.users.phone are plain text, and subscriptions/commercial_subscriptions.stripe_customer_id/stripe_subscription_id (the actual 'billing identifiers') are plain text protected by RLS, not column encryption -- confirmed false as stated, corrected to name the one field that IS encrypted and accurately describe billing IDs as RLS-protected opaque references, not encrypted. (2) 'TLS 1.3 enforced on all endpoints (HSTS preload)' -- ran a same-origin fetch('/') from the live production page and read response.headers.get('strict-transport-security'): returned null. No HSTS header is sent at all, let alone an actual preload-list submission (a real, separate process via hstspreload.org) -- confirmed false, corrected to the accurate, still-true claim (HTTPS/TLS enforced). Separately, src/components/landing/TrustStrip.tsx (rendered live on the homepage, not dead code) asserted a bare 'GDPR & CCPA compliant' badge -- reworded to 'GDPR & CCPA rights supported', matching the real, verifiable mechanism Security.tsx itself describes (export/deletion requests via email), not an unqualified legal-compliance certification this codebase has no way to substantiate. Also reworded TrustStrip's '97,500+ verified benchmarks' to 'benchmark data points' for the same self-certification reason already fixed elsewhere this session (QNT-DEFECT-025) -- these are internally-modeled/derived per canonical-facts.ts's own prior correction (P0-24), not independently verified per-row. NOT fixed: src/components/landing/SecurityBadges.tsx has the same false 'GDPR Compliant'/'EU Data Centers, Data never leaves EU' claims (the latter directly contradicted by get_project confirming the Supabase project region is us-east-1, not EU) -- left as-is because the component has zero consumers anywhere in the app (dead code); flagged so it isn't wired up later without someone noticing the false claims already inside it.
affected_files: src/components/landing/SecurityBadges.tsx (known-unfixed dependency -- dead code, not corrected, see next_action)
defects.next_action: Status is IMPLEMENTED_NOT_DEPLOYED, not VERIFIED_COMPLETE (CodeRabbit correctly caught this on PR #62, same class of miss as QNT-DEFECT-027) -- the source fix is committed, but the pre-fix infrastructure checks (SQL query, live HTTP header read) were run against the CURRENT production state, which still serves the OLD, false copy until the Vercel deploy pipeline (QNT-DEFECT-002) is unblocked and a real deploy ships this branch. Promote to VERIFIED_COMPLETE only after re-running the same live HTTP header / page-text check against production post-deploy. Separately: if src/components/landing/SecurityBadges.tsx is ever wired into a route, its GDPR/EU-data-center claims must be corrected or removed first -- do not assume it's safe just because it compiles.

defects.title: 3 more live, bare 'GDPR/CCPA Compliant' claims found in a repo-wide sweep after QNT-DEFECT-029 -- FAQSection.tsx, Footer.tsx (every page), and UpgradePrompt.tsx (the paywall modal)
defects.detail: QNT-DEFECT-029 fixed the 2 instances found while investigating Security.tsx specifically. A follow-up repo-wide grep for GDPR/CCPA found 3 more live, real (not dead-code) instances of the same bare-compliance-claim pattern: (1) FAQSection.tsx (lazy-loaded onto the homepage, Landing.tsx) answered 'How is my data protected?' with 'We are GDPR and CCPA compliant' plus 'AES-256-GCM encryption... in transit' (in-transit encryption is TLS, not AES-256-GCM -- that cipher is the at-rest scheme; conflating the two in one sentence was also imprecise). (2) Footer.tsx -- rendered on literally every page -- had a bare 'GDPR & CCPA Compliant' line. (3) UpgradePrompt.tsx, the live paywall/upgrade modal shown across the app (AppDashboard.tsx, useOnboarding.ts, DocGeneratorPanel.tsx), had a bare 'GDPR compliant' trust chip. All 3 reworded to describe the real, verifiable mechanism (data export/deletion rights supported) rather than asserting a legal certification status this codebase has no way to substantiate, consistent with the QNT-DEFECT-029 fix. Also found, NOT fixed: src/components/landing/TrustLogos.tsx has the identical 'GDPR Compliant' claim but -- like SecurityBadges.tsx before it -- has zero consumers anywhere in the app (confirmed via grep for its import), so it's dead code with no live exposure; flagged rather than touched.
affected_files: src/components/landing/TrustLogos.tsx (known-unfixed dependency -- dead code, not corrected)
defects.next_action: Status is IMPLEMENTED_NOT_DEPLOYED for the same reason as QNT-DEFECT-027/029 -- source fix committed, blocked on the QNT-DEFECT-002 deploy pipeline before it's live. Promote to VERIFIED_COMPLETE only after a post-deploy re-check. If TrustLogos.tsx or SecurityBadges.tsx is ever wired into a live route, both must be corrected first. Ran the exhaustive follow-up sweep this same pass (grep for compliant|certified|ISO 27001|SOC 2 across all of src/, not scoped to files already touched): the only other 'compliant' hit on a live surface is FAQSection.tsx's 'PCI-DSS compliant' (Stripe payment processing) -- left as-is since it's standard and accurate for a Stripe-integrated merchant that never handles raw card data (Privacy.tsx already correctly attributes PCI-DSS to Stripe, not Quantis). All other hits are either the already-flagged dead code (SecurityBadges.tsx, TrustLogos.tsx), already-reviewed-and-fine scoped claims (TrustStrip.tsx's 'in prep', RouteSEO.tsx's 'GDPR-compliant deletion'), or unrelated content about third-party certifications in example/blog copy (ASE-certified mechanics, certified org charts in an AML blog post) that make no claim about Quantis itself. CodeRabbit caught a real additional overclaim in the SAME FAQSection.tsx answer this fix touched: it said Quantis 'never share[s]... your business ideas or analysis data to third parties', which is false given DeepSeek and Anthropic Claude (both disclosed third-party AI processors per QNT-DEFECT-024/Privacy.tsx) genuinely receive the idea text to perform the analysis. Fixed in the same commit: narrowed the claim to 'never sell', and explicitly named the AI processing partners with a pointer to the Privacy Policy.

defects.title: Root cause of the CLI-based one-click Vercel deploy failing was git commit-author EMAIL, not token/scope/org-ID -- every commit this session was authored under an email Vercel can't match to a GitHub account
defects.detail: After QNT-DEFECT-002/027/029's fixes (secrets scoped correctly, VERCEL_ORG_ID/VERCEL_PROJECT_ID verified against Vercel's own API, --scope aiwmc flag added then removed after it caused a separate 'User not found' error), the CLI deploy workflow finally progressed past 'Pull Vercel project settings' and reached an actual Vercel deployment record -- but Vercel's dashboard then showed 'Deployment Blocked: the commit email AIWMCSRM@gmail.com could not be matched to a GitHub account.' This is a DIFFERENT check than the original git-integration block (which keys off the pushing GitHub identity/AIWMCX): this one keys off the COMMIT AUTHOR EMAIL embedded in the git commit object itself, which Vercel's CLI-deploy path also enforces. Checked git config directly: this session's environment had global user.email set to AIWMCSRM@gmail.com (a real, legitimate staff email per is_content_admin_allowlisted(), just not one linked to any Vercel-recognized GitHub account) -- meaning every commit authored in this session across all 10+ PRs (#58-#68) carries this email, not the founder email (jeltovbogdan@gmail.com) that actually has Vercel access. Corrected git config user.email (both --local and --global) to jeltovbogdan@gmail.com per explicit user confirmation of the correct address, then made this commit under the corrected identity so a fresh HEAD exists for the next deploy attempt to use.
defects.next_action: IMPORTANT FOLLOW-UP FINDING: fixing local git config was NOT sufficient by itself. After merging that fix via `gh pr merge --squash`, main's new HEAD (12a0a59c) was STILL authored as AIWMCSRM@gmail.com -- squash-merging via the GitHub API creates a brand-new commit authored by whatever identity the merge API call itself uses, discarding the original commit's (correctly-authored) author entirely. Testing whether `gh pr merge --rebase` (which reapplies the original commits rather than synthesizing a new one) preserves the corrected author instead. If confirmed, every future merge to main intended to reach Vercel must use --rebase (or --merge), never --squash, until/unless the underlying GitHub-account-level identity (whatever account `gh` authenticates as) has its own primary email corrected -- that would fix squash-merges too, but requires changing the GitHub account's own settings, not just local git config.
